metadata._mix_note: visual_mix and treatment_counts are counted from `role`, so an authored texture_field is reported separately from an authored scene. raw_treatment_counts is the `treatment` field as the buildability gate reads it, where an authored texture is a graphic because it is drawn rather than sourced.
metadata._clock: Slots are laid on the MEASURED narration: each paragraph's span is its own wav plus the air the script wrote after it. script_total_seconds is the planned clock the duration band was agreed against, kept for comparison.
metadata._description_is_the_brief: A slot's `description` is what the sentence NEEDS to see - the brief written before any asset existed. `asset_title` is the Commons file that was actually assigned to it. The two do not always say the same thing, because assignment is by subject family and plate size rather than by matching prose to a picture, and the gap is visible rather than hidden: every assigned pick was looked at beside its brief (projects/king-tut/review_picks.py -> renders/picks_*.png) and the ones that were wrong about their SUBJECT, as opposed to merely different from the brief, are named in artifacts/rejected_assets.json with the reason. None of these descriptions is rendered on screen: a sourced still carries only its provider and licence, so a brief that differs from its plate is an imprecise record and not a false caption.

rejected_assets._why: Assets rejected BY EYE after looking at every assigned pick beside the slot that asked for it (projects/king-tut/review_picks.py, renders/picks_*.png). Filename filtering cannot tell a photograph of a tomb wall from a photograph of the tourist information board standing in front of it: both are called 'KV62, Egypt 11.jpg'. The playbook's rule is that a candidate must share a word with the slot AND the slot must independently be about that subject, and that validating an asset against the subject the matcher itself chose is circular. So this is the non-circular half: a human-equivalent look at the picture.

degradations.what: The film's one map_route slot (act2_s016) draws on the flat plate, not on the terrain base the playbook's visual_cadence.maps section asks for.
degradations.why: assets/basemaps/NE2_HR_LC_SR/ is not on this machine. The source is a 700 MB public-domain Natural Earth raster and fetching it needs network access this unattended session was not granted.
degradations.flagged_before: The script-stage review raised it as a nitpick: 'Needs assets/basemaps/NE2_HR_LC_SR/ before scene_plan commits a map slot.'
degradations.why_the_slot_was_kept: The beat is a geographic claim - twenty candidate meteorites within two thousand kilometres of the Red Sea, one of them Kharga - and the component draws real world-atlas coastlines and borders, so Egypt, the Nile, the Red Sea and Arabia all read. This is not run #1's defect, which was a route crossing a sea with nothing on screen saying so. One slot in 174.
